title: Claw-back of Government Incentives Made to Companies
what_it_is: Claw-back of Government Incentives Made to Companies

sections.label: Clawed back Government incentives
sections.summary: The Minister was asked how often Government incentives were clawed back in the last five years and the main reasons, which were largely non-fulfilment of deliverables or non-compliance with terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) how many times were awarded Government incentives clawed back from companies in each of the last five years; and (b) what were the main reasons for the claw-backs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This made up less than 1% of total incentive cases over the same period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: These cases were largely attributed to non-fulfilment of deliverables or non-compliance with terms and conditions that were set out before the commencement of the projects.

sections.label: External auditors and incentive compliance
sections.summary: The Minister said external auditors generally opine on whether accounts are true and fair, not on compliance with incentive conditions, and claw-backs are a fraction of 1% of awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Member's point on external auditors, the remit of external auditors, in general, is, as the Member would appreciate, to render an opinion as to whether the accounts of the company are true and fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is not really about ascertaining compliance with conditions attached to Government's incentives and grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: However, if the auditors themselves are prepared to do it further, it is not costless.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The question then is who bears the cost of doing that.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But I think it is an idea we can think about.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In general, I want to make a point that, as I have said in my reply, these claw-backs constitute a fraction of 1% of all such awards.
